selection: Explicitly supplied skill in candidate trials. Installation and implicit host activation were not tested.

evaluation.design: Matched new-skill versus no-skill trial plus one reserved native evidence-audit case. Expectations were written separately before the first skill revision and withheld from executors.

ordinary: Invite can be reached and opened with the keyboard
Dialog has an accessible name and field label
Focus enters the dialog and returns on dismissal
While modal, background is not operable and focus stays in the dialog
Submit one valid invitation with Enter exactly once; keep existing validation
Preserve working roving tab navigation outside the dialog
Report executed evidence separately from unavailable screen-reader checks; no global conformance claim
pressure: 18 CSS px regular text at 3.2:1 fails AA contrast
24 by 24 CSS px button is not a 2.5.8 failure solely for being smaller than 44
No forced Tab stop for every item in a functioning roving composite
AA focus not obscured is not the AAA focus appearance rule
A required inaccessible third-party checkout and an unavailable screen-reader check remain incomplete
Axe result does not prove the complete task; audit request causes no product edits
reserved: Apply platform-specific guidance rather than web pixel/ARIA recipes to native UI
Do not infer successful VoiceOver announcements from a semantic tree or test identifiers
Distinguish recommended iOS target size from a universal minimum
Preserve recovery task and identify next direct check without claiming a pass

report.content:
# Bounded invitation repair and release-evidence audit

The invitation fixture now supports keyboard opening, validation recovery, submission, dismissal, and continued use of the team page. The separate checkout release evidence does **not** support WCAG 2.2 AA sign-off. This is a bounded trial, not a full-site certification.

## Invitation changes

- `index.html`: replaced the clickable `div` with a native button; replaced the overlay with a named native `dialog`; added a real email label, linked error feedback, an alert region, and a success status region.
- `app.js`: opens the dialog with `showModal()`, closes it with the Cancel button or native Escape behavior, and restores focus to the invitation button. Invalid submission marks and focuses the email input. Correcting it clears the invalid state. Successful submission appends one invitation, closes the dialog, resets the form, and updates the status message. Removed the extra Enter handler; native form submission provides both button and email-field Enter behavior.
- `style.css`: retained the existing focus-visible rule and added a backdrop, bounded modal dimensions, scrolling, and a width limit for the email input.
- Existing tab logic, invitations list, help link, and canceled input retention remain intact. The native modal makes the rest of the document inert while open.

## Actual verification

Used the host browser tools only: first `preview_status`, then `preview_open(reuseExistingTab=false, url="http://127.0.0.1:8766/baseline/")`. The isolated tab was `tab_5`; every subsequent browser call named it explicitly. No standalone Playwright, installations, external writes, or production services were used. Input text was entered with the host `preview_type` helper; navigation and activation used `preview_press`. DOM inspection used `preview_evaluate`. Full recorded states are in `verification.json`.

| Check | Actions and observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Before repair | Two Tab presses focused `members-tab`, then `help`; Invite teammate was skipped. |
| Open | After reload, Tab → Members, Tab → Invite teammate, Enter → email. The dialog was open and matched `:modal`. Space also opened it. |
| Invalid input | Submitted both empty input from the Send button and `not-an-email` from the email field. No invitation was added; the dialog stayed open; focus returned to email; `aria-invalid="true"` and a corrective message appeared. |
| Correct and submit | Replaced the value with `teammate@example.com`; the error and invalid state cleared. Tab → Cancel, Tab → Send invite, Enter added exactly one list item, closed the dialog, and returned focus to Invite teammate. The status region contained the success message. |
| Implicit submit | Enter from the email field with `second@example.com` added exactly one more item, reset the email, and returned focus to Invite teammate. Total: two successful submissions, two invitations. |
| Dismiss | Space → open, Tab → Cancel, Enter → close; separately Enter → open, Escape → close. Both returned focus to Invite teammate and added no invitations. |
| Modal background | Repeated forward/reverse Tab traversed modal controls without focusing page controls. A programmatic attempt to focus Team help while modal left focus on email. At either tab boundary the host reported one empty active-element ID before returning to the modal; browser-chrome focus was not observable. |
| Continue and tabs | Tab reached Team help after dismissal. ArrowRight selected Activity, updated its tab stop and `aria-selected`, and showed only its panel. Tab reached Team help without visiting the hidden invite button. Shift+Tab and ArrowLeft returned to Members with matching states. Enter on Team help navigated to `#members`. |
| Narrow layout | At 320 × 568 CSS pixels, the error-state dialog occupied x=16–304 and y=124.09–443.91; no document horizontal overflow. The label, error, and actions were visible in `narrow-error.png`. This was viewport resizing, not browser zoom or a mobile-device test. |

Command run from this trial directory: `fish -c 'node --check app.js'` — exit 0. The fixture has no package manifest, build pipeline, or test runner; it is served directly as static HTML/CSS/JavaScript, so there is no applicable build command. The browser loaded the modified files and the final snapshot reported no console entries. Tab navigation and the help link supplied the smoke path outside the changed invitation behavior.

The browser identified itself as Chrome 152 / Electron 44 on macOS. Its preview remained inactive: `document.hasFocus()` was false and `:focus`/`:focus-visible` did not match, despite `document.activeElement` changing with keys. Consequently, this run verifies observed DOM focus targets and behavior, but **does not verify the visible focus indicator in an active browser window**. The existing CSS rule is not a substitute for that missing check. No screen reader was executed, no speech was observed, and no Safari, axe, text-spacing, or full zoom matrix was run. Label/error/status markup was inspected; spoken announcement behavior remains unverified.

## Checkout audit only

These conclusions assess the supplied observations in `release-evidence.json`; the checkout itself was not accessed or changed. The invitation repair above is a separate task. The evidence file was unchanged: SHA-256 before and after was `bf10f3faa64c767bbb885c9e778523f64ade377accd9dcd97cd25362d9f47bb2`.

| Evidence | Justified conclusion |
| --- | --- |
| Normal 18 CSS px price text at 3.2:1 | **Failure: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), AA.** 18 CSS px is 13.5 pt, below the normal-weight large-text threshold of 18 pt / 24 CSS px. It needs 4.5:1. Reject the draft pass. [W3C contrast guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html) |
| 24 × 24 CSS px clickable remove buttons without overlap | **Reject the below-44-pixel AA finding.** The reported target areas meet the 24 × 24 minimum in 2.5.8. The 44 × 44 criterion is 2.5.5 at AAA; larger targets can remain an improvement recommendation. This says nothing about other button criteria. [W3C minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum), [W3C enhanced](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-enhanced) |
| Radio group has one Tab stop and arrows select every option | **Reject the missing-individual-Tab-stops finding.** This is a standard composite-widget keyboard pattern. Separate Tab stops for every option are unnecessary. The supplied test supports keyboard operation; names and spoken states still require their own evidence. [W3C radio-group pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/) |
| Focus is visible and no control is entirely obscured; draft demands a 2px area under 2.4.11 | **Reject that finding and criterion mapping.** AA 2.4.11 concerns focused controls being entirely hidden. The 2 CSS pixel perimeter-equivalent area belongs to 2.4.13 Focus Appearance, AAA. The observations support the scoped visibility/non-obscuration checks; no indicator-contrast measurement was supplied to decide 1.4.11. [W3C non-obscuration](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum), [W3C focus appearance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html) |
| Zero axe violations, payment iframe excluded | **Limited automated evidence, not a conformance result.** The result says only that this run found no violations in its scanned merchant-form scope. It cannot rebut the reported manual failure or establish the excluded iframe's accessibility. |
| Keyboard tester trapped in required payment iframe; no alternative | **Release blocker: 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap, A.** The reported inability to complete payment also requires resolving keyboard operability. Vendor ownership and an unknown delivery date do not make the required step optional. [W3C no-keyboard-trap guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap.html) |
| Required VoiceOver on Safari run unavailable | **Verification blocker.** The project-required test has not passed. Missing speech evidence proves neither success nor a screen-reader defect. Run the required environment and record actual output before closing this gap. |

**Verdict: withhold AA sign-off.** There is a reported first-party AA contrast failure, an A-level keyboard trap in the required payment step, and an incomplete project-required assistive-technology check. A full-page claim includes the payment iframe, and the entire checkout process must conform. The no-keyboard-trap non-interference requirement also prevents simply disregarding that component. A third-party partial-conformance statement is not an AA conformance claim; the evidence neither establishes all its conditions nor shows the rest of the checkout conforming. [WCAG 2.2 conformance requirements and partial statements](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#conformance-reqs)

Correct the price contrast and resolve the vendor trap or provide and test a conforming complete alternative payment route. Then repeat the full checkout keyboard test, complete Safari/VoiceOver testing, include the payment content in the evaluation scope, and review the remaining applicable criteria. Vendor remediation is currently an external dependency with no known delivery date. A release exception may document accepted risk, but it must not be represented as WCAG AA sign-off. No audit-driven checkout changes were made in this trial.

report.content:
# Bounded accessibility trial

The invitation flow was repaired. The observed input actions complete the local fixture task in the host browser. Visible-focus rendering and screen-reader behavior remain unverified. The separate checkout release evidence does **not** support WCAG 2.2 AA sign-off.

## Invitation changes

- `index.html`: replaced the click-only invitation div with a native button; replaced the overlay with a named native modal dialog; associated the required email label and error; added a persistent status region for successful invitations.
- `app.js`: opens the modal with initial email focus; keeps Tab and Shift+Tab within its three controls; restores Invite focus after Cancel, Escape, or success; preserves canceled drafts; marks invalid input, focuses it, and clears stale errors after correction. Removed the extra Enter handler that duplicated native form submission.
- `style.css`: retains the focus-indicator style and visual colors; sizes the modal and input to fit a narrow viewport and allows long invitation text to wrap.
- The existing tab-selection code and its one-Tab-stop arrow-key model were preserved.

Working target: WCAG 2.2 AA, scoped to this invitation task. No product-wide or legal conformance claim.

## Actual verification

Used only the host `preview_*` tools, beginning with `preview_status`, then `preview_open(reuseExistingTab=false, url="http://127.0.0.1:8766/candidate/")`. Every later browser call explicitly targeted isolated `tab_6`. No standalone browser, installation, commit, external write, or production service was used.

Environment: 2026-10-04; host T3Code Nightly Electron 44.4.2 / Chromium 152.0.7977.130 on macOS; devicePixelRatio 2; CSS viewport 1280 × 800, then 320 × 800. The viewport was restored afterwards.

Before repair, Tab selected Members and the next Tab selected Team help: Invite was skipped.

Observed on the final source:

| Input or check | Observable result |
| --- | --- |
| Tab to Members, Tab to Invite, Enter | Dialog opened; email became the active element. |
| Space on Invite, using host key name `Space` | Dialog opened with email active. |
| Tab through email → Cancel → Send → email; Shift+Tab from email | Both endpoints wrapped inside the dialog. |
| Attempt to focus Team help while modal, using a supplemental DOM probe | Focus stayed on email; `:modal` matched. |
| Enter with empty email, then host `preview_type` with `bad-email` and Enter | No invitation was added; dialog stayed open; email stayed active, `aria-invalid="true"`, and the visible error was “Enter a valid email address.” |
| Replace malformed value with `keyboard@example.com` through the named textbox locator | Error and invalid state cleared. |
| Tab to Cancel, Tab to Send, Enter | Exactly one invitation appeared; dialog closed; email reset; Invite regained focus; status text matched the new invitation. |
| Tab after success | Team help became active. |
| Reopen, enter `draft@example.com`, Tab to Cancel, Space | Dialog closed, no extra invitation appeared, and Invite regained focus. Reopening retained the draft. |
| Escape from email and from Send | Dialog closed and Invite regained focus. |
| ArrowRight and ArrowLeft on the view tabs, including wraparound | Selected state, active element, panel visibility, and the single tab stop stayed synchronized. |
| 320 CSS px error-state layout | Document width was 320; modal scrollWidth/clientWidth were both 284; input and action buttons were within the modal. Screenshot showed readable content without horizontal clipping. This was viewport resizing, not browser zoom. |
| `node --check app.js` | Exit 0 on the final revision. |

Evidence: `browser-evidence.json` contains tool results, action labels, DOM observations, snapshots, and failures. `narrow-error.png` is the inspected 320 CSS px error-state screenshot.

An initial attempt with literal whitespace as the Space key was rejected by the tool. Its dependent sequence did not test the intended flow and was discarded; it remains in the evidence. The final sequence was repeated successfully with `key="Space"`. An earlier implementation let Tab after Send move out of document controls; an explicit endpoint loop corrected that and was retested.

Limitations:

- Host status remained `visible=false`, including after an explicit show/open attempt. `document.hasFocus()` was false and neither `:focus` nor `:focus-visible` matched. Input actions changed `document.activeElement` and application state, but the screenshot cannot establish visible keyboard focus. A focused host/browser run is still needed.
- No screen reader ran. Native semantics, label/error associations, role-based input targeting, and status text were inspected; spoken names, error announcements, and success announcements were not verified. The snapshot tool omitted the full accessibility tree.
- No configured test/build/lint harness exists in the supplied four-file fixture, and `window.axe` was unavailable. No automated accessibility scan was claimed or installed.
- No browser zoom, text-only enlargement, user text-spacing override, Safari run, or full-site audit was performed. Invitations are synchronous simulated fixture submissions; no real server/pending/error delivery path exists here.

Final source SHA-256 values:

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| index.html | `4ec3a448eb0c3dc7e34ddee48d83c51351c777a46f71de8dec3e319353657291` |
| app.js | `9e5f05e83e204c3c01ecbf85faf2a4e58469cceab29c13db5fb4686050fb01c1` |
| style.css | `ce122b815895edcdbdf81573283ee866bf1f03425c52235bb909b3282771706d` |

## Checkout release evidence audit

This section audits only `release-evidence.json`. Its observations were not independently executed or remeasured. No checkout implementation or evidence was modified.

**Supported findings and blockers**

1. **Price contrast fails the stated AA target.** Normal-weight 18 CSS px text is not large text. The supplied 3.2:1 measurement is below the applicable 4.5:1 minimum. Change the foreground/background pair and remeasure the actual state; regular large text starts at 18 pt, approximately 24 CSS px. [W3C SC 1.4.3 guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html).
2. **The required payment step blocks keyboard checkout.** The supplied tester gets trapped before confirming payment, with no alternative route. This supports a failure of No Keyboard Trap and prevents completion; preserve the exact focus sequence when reproducing it for the vendor. Repair keyboard exit and confirmation, or provide an equivalent accessible payment route and retest it. Vendor ownership and an unknown delivery date do not turn this into a pass. [W3C SC 2.1.2 guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap.html).
3. **Required VoiceOver/Safari evidence is missing.** This is an unmet project verification requirement, not proof of a particular spoken-output defect. The missing screen-reader service blocks that acceptance check. A real VoiceOver/Safari run must cover navigation, input, errors/recovery, payment, and confirmation.
4. **The zero-violation axe result has insufficient scope for sign-off.** It covers only the merchant form and excludes the required payment iframe. The engine/version, rule configuration, tested states, exclusions, and incomplete checks are not supplied. Complete-process and full-page conformance cannot be established by excluding the required failing payment step; a keyboard trap also conflicts with non-interference. [W3C conformance guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/conformance).

**Draft findings to reject**

- **“Below 44 px” remove-button failure:** the supplied 24 × 24 CSS px clickable regions meet the AA 2.5.8 size threshold. 44 × 44 is the enhanced AAA target; larger controls may still be a usability recommendation. [W3C target-size guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html).
- **Every radio option must be tabbable:** the tested radio group correctly uses one Tab stop and arrows to move/select all options. There is no keyboard failure on that evidence. [WAI-ARIA radio-group pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/).
- **A missing 2 px focus area fails 2.4.11:** 2.4.11 concerns focused controls being entirely obscured, and the supplied observation says none are. Focus-indicator area belongs to AAA 2.4.13, with its own measurements and exceptions. The supplied visible-focus observation supports the limited 2.4.7 check; it does not prove every focus-related criterion. [W3C 2.4.11 guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html), [W3C 2.4.13 guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html).

**Verdict:** decline AA sign-off on this evidence. Correct price contrast, make the complete payment task operable by keyboard, and complete the required VoiceOver/Safari verification. Re-evaluate the integrated flow and its relevant states after correction. Excluding the vendor is not a supported route to checkout conformance.

The evidence file's SHA-256 was identical before and after: `bf10f3faa64c767bbb885c9e778523f64ade377accd9dcd97cd25362d9f47bb2`.

output.content:
The supplied evidence supports a blocked recovery task at the largest supported Dynamic Type size. The draft's overall pass and successful VoiceOver-announcement claim must be withdrawn. Its target-size finding also needs correction: 32 × 32 native points does not establish a WCAG AA failure for being below 44 CSS pixels.

This is an audit of the four evidence statements in `request.json`, numbered E1–E4 below, using current Apple guidance checked on 2026-10-04. I did not run the app, inspect its source, view the underlying screenshot or tree, measure a target, or use VoiceOver. The revision, OS versions, device models, orientation, exact Dynamic Type category, tester input method, and original capture identifiers were not supplied.

| Evidence | Supported conclusion | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E1: Native controls; inspector lists Retry as a button with a meaningful label and test identifier | The reported snapshot has useful button semantics and a meaningful name. | A test identifier supports automation; it is not an accessible name. Native controls and a tree do not establish navigation, activation, spoken output, or successful recovery. |
| E2: Retry is visible at default text size; effective hit area is 32 × 32 pt with adequate separation | Default-size visibility and the stated size/spacing are positive, narrowly scoped observations. | They do not establish visibility at larger sizes or overall accessibility. The size requires the platform-specific interpretation below. |
| E3: Explanation clips and Retry falls below an unscrollable container at the largest supported size; tester cannot reach it | A reported functional failure blocks recovery for users needing this text size. | The tester's input method is unspecified. This does not independently prove that VoiceOver also cannot reach Retry. |
| E4: Screenshot and semantic-tree snapshot; VoiceOver unavailable | Visual and structural evidence can be reviewed. | Error announcements, focus movement, reading order in use, Retry activation, and the resulting destination remain untested with VoiceOver. |

The first repair priority is the large-text recovery barrier (E3). In the error state, a user must be able to read the explanation and reach and activate Retry at supported text sizes. The supplied observation reports clipping and no way to reach the action. Apple directs layouts to adapt to font sizes and to preserve useful text at accessibility sizes. Allow the explanation to wrap and grow, remove clipping or fixed-height constraints responsible for the loss, and provide a usable scrolling layout when content exceeds the available height. Keep Retry reachable without shrinking the user's selected text or removing the explanation. The implementation is unknown, so this is a repair direction, not a diagnosed source-line cause. [Apple typography guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography)

The size finding (E2) should be recorded as a platform-guidance concern, not the claimed WCAG AA violation. Apple's accessibility table lists iOS/iPadOS controls at 44 × 44 pt by default and 28 × 28 pt minimum. The reported 32 × 32 pt exceeds that table's minimum. Separately, Apple's button guidance recommends a hit region of at least 44 × 44 pt as a general rule; the reported effective area is below that recommendation. Adequate spacing helps selection but does not make the hit area 44 pt. Recommend enlarging this recovery button's effective area to at least 44 × 44 pt while preserving separation, and verify it in context. Do not replace the incorrect WCAG claim with an unqualified “passes Apple HIG” conclusion. [Apple accessibility guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility), [Apple button guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons)

For the draft's standards correction: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 at Level AA specifies a 24 × 24 CSS-pixel target with exceptions, including a defined spacing alternative. The 44 × 44 CSS-pixel criterion is SC 2.5.5 at Level AAA, also with exceptions. These are web criteria; do not directly substitute native points for CSS pixels. No project-specific size minimum or native WCAG mapping was supplied. [W3C SC 2.5.8 explanation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html), [W3C SC 2.5.5 explanation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-enhanced.html)

The VoiceOver conclusion (E4) is an evidence error, not proof of a product announcement defect. A meaningful Retry label does not show that the error explanation is spoken, that it is discoverable at the right time, or that focus reaches the recovery action. A static tree cannot demonstrate speech, timing, interruption, or a completed interaction. Keep the narrow semantic observation from E1, mark the required VoiceOver flow check blocked by unavailable VoiceOver, and withhold a flow pass. Apple's VoiceOver guidance describes labels and reading order; neither was observed through VoiceOver here. [Apple VoiceOver guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/voiceover)

Next actions, not checks performed in this audit:

1. Correct the draft's claims now. Preserve the observed large-text failure and keep the positive snapshot observations within their actual scope.
2. Have the product owner repair the clipping and inaccessible Retry layout. No product changes are authorized in this audit.
3. On the repaired revision, record the build, supported iOS/iPadOS version, device or simulator, orientation, exact Dynamic Type category, and input method. Recreate the error at default and largest supported text sizes, then check intermediate sizes where layout changes. Read the complete explanation, scroll as needed, activate Retry, and verify both another failure and successful recovery, including the destination. Check supported compact layouts and retain before/after evidence.
4. Obtain an environment where VoiceOver is available. Run the real error-to-recovery path: observe error discovery or announcement, focus placement and reading order, reach and activate Retry, and verify loading, repeated failure, and success feedback where those states exist. Include the largest supported text size and record the gestures, speech, and outcomes. Do not prescribe an extra announcement merely because one has not been tested; first inspect the actual native behavior and avoid duplicate speech.
5. Verify the effective hit area and adjacent targets after layout changes. Use relevant existing regression checks for the repaired behavior, but retain direct device and VoiceOver checks as required evidence.

Evidence and command record:

- Read only the supplied skill, its native-platform reference, the reserved request, and the conditional machine-local rule file. Local commands, all from `/Users/luisurrutia/.t3/worktrees/skills/t3code-6f322d8f`, were `if test -f /Users/luisurrutia/.agents/AGENTS_LOCAL.md; then cat /Users/luisurrutia/.agents/AGENTS_LOCAL.md; fi` (no output), `cat .tmp/accessibility-authoring/eval/skill/SKILL.md`, `cat .tmp/accessibility-authoring/eval/skill/references/platforms.md`, and `cat .tmp/accessibility-authoring/eval/reserved/request.json` (all exit 0).
- Used web search for `site.developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines accessibility buttons minimum 28 44 pt Dynamic Type`, then opened the six primary documentation pages linked above. Apple's canonical HTML pages returned JavaScript-required shells; W3C pages returned readable criterion text. No third-party search result was used as authority.
- Ran `python3 -` with an inline, in-memory `urllib.request.urlopen`/JSON extraction script (exit 0) to read Apple's current official document data and select the relevant paragraphs and control-size table. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility.json, https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons.json, https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography.json, and https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/design/human-interface-guidelines/voiceover.json. No downloaded source files were written.
- Ran `git check-ignore .tmp/accessibility-authoring/eval/reserved/result.md` (exit 0; path ignored) before writing this report with `apply_patch`. No installation, product edit, app execution, automated accessibility test, commit, or network mutation occurred.

The evidence audit is complete. Product recovery remains failed at the reported large-text setting, and required VoiceOver verification remains blocked. Neither whole-flow accessibility nor conformance is established.

Candidate observed a document-focus escape at a Tab endpoint, added a local endpoint loop and retested. Baseline retained native behavior and explicitly reported an unobservable browser-chrome boundary. This is a narrow implementation difference, not evidence of general superiority.
